content.text: When the built-in
fields
don't fit your content, create your own. A custom field has two parts: a constructor function that you call in your schema, and a React component that renders the field in the dashboard.
Create a field
The constructor describes the value the field stores and its options, and points to the component that renders it:

`Field.Create<Value, Options>` is the type of a field that stores `Value` (anything JSON can hold) and accepts your `Options` next to the standard ones: `initialValue`, `required`, `readOnly`, `hidden`, `shared`, `validate` and `width`, the width of the field in the entry form. Queries return the stored value as it is.
To describe the options as an interface, extend `FieldOptions` from `alinea/core` and type the options argument with `WithoutLabel`:
`Field.create` takes:
`label`: the label of the field.
`options`: the options passed to your constructor.
`view`: the component that renders the field, see
Point to the view
`defaultValue`: a function returning the value of new entries, when the field has no `initialValue`.
`searchableText`: a function returning the text of a value to include in the dashboard search.
Render the field

The view receives the field as its `field` prop. Hooks from `alinea/cms` read and write its value, and `FieldChrome` renders the label, help text, shared badge and validation error around your control, like the built-in fields do:
`FieldChrome` takes the `label`, the `help` option, `required`, `readOnly` and `shared` from the field's options and the message from its validation. Pass any of these as a prop to override it.
Use the field in a type like any other:
`useFieldOptions` returns the options with the dashboard's state applied: `readOnly` is also `true` when the user's
role
can't edit the field or the entry is not editable, so respect it in your view.
Point to the view

`view` is usually a module path, resolved from your project root with the path aliases of your `tsconfig.json`. The default export is used, append `#Name` for a named export: `'@/fields/Priority.view#PriorityView'`.

A path keeps dashboard code out of your site: your schema is imported by your pages and server components, and the view is only loaded by the dashboard. You can pass a component instead (`view: RangeView`), but then the component and the `alinea/cms` hooks it imports end up everywhere your schema is imported, including server components where they can't run. Use a path unless the field is only used in scripts.
Build views with the dashboard components
`alinea/cms` holds what is tied to the CMS: the hooks, `FieldChrome` and the view prop types. The generic building blocks are in
`alinea/components`
. Its form controls take the same `label`, `description`, `error`, `required`, `readOnly` and `shared` props and render their own chrome, so a field built on one of them looks native:

The entry editor sets `--alinea-header-height` to the height of its header. A view that fills the visible editor can size itself with it, for example `height: calc(100dvh - var(--alinea-header-height))`.
Style your own markup with the
theme tokens
, such as `--alinea-fg-muted`, `--alinea-border` and `--alinea-radius`, so it follows light and dark mode. `--alinea-workspace-color` holds the `color` of the current workspace.
The alinea/cms API

Everything in `alinea/cms` works in field views and in the other components the dashboard renders for an entry: `Field.view` sections, entry `actions` and a type's `view`. A root's `view` is not part of an entry: the hooks that read the dashboard, such as `useGraph`, `useNavigate`, `useLocale` and `useUser`, and `EntryTable` work there, the field hooks, `EditField` and `EditFields` don't, and `useEntry()` returns `null`.
Field hooks, for the field passed to a view or another field of the same entry, list row or object:
`useField(field)`: the stored value and a setter, like `useState`. The setter also accepts an updater function.
`useFieldValue(field)`, `useFieldSetter(field)`: only the value, or only the setter.
`useFieldOptions(field)`: the field's options, including `label` and the resolved `readOnly` and `hidden`.
`useFieldError(field)`: the validation message from `required` or `validate`, if any.
`useFieldKey(field)`: the key the field is stored under, such as `'title'`.

Other fields: pass any field of the same list row or object, of a parent row or of the entry to these hooks, it resolves in the nearest scope that holds it. Import the type from your schema (`useFieldValue(BlogPost.title)`) or pass the field through your field's options. A view shared by types that each define their own field passes its key instead: `useFieldValue('path')` reads that field of the same row, untyped. `useSiblingFieldValue(key)` is deprecated.
A field in the rows of a list can read a field of the entry, here to suggest the post title as a caption:
Entry and dashboard hooks:

`useEntry()`: the entry being edited, with its `id`, `type`, `title`, `path`, `url`, `locale`, `status`, `workspace`, `root`, `parentId` and `data`. `data` holds the field values as saved, read the live value of a field while it is edited with `useFieldValue(field)`. `null` outside an entry.
`useLocale()`: the locale being edited, or `null` for content without translations.
`useGraph()`: query content from the dashboard with the same API as `cms`, for example to list entries in a picker.
`useUser()`, `usePolicy()`: the signed-in user and their
permissions

`useNavigate()`: returns a function that opens an entry or root in the dashboard: `navigate({entryId, locale})` looks up the entry's workspace and root, `navigate({workspace, root})` opens a root. Pass `view: 'edit'` or `view: 'overview'` to pick the form or the list of children. The editor is asked to confirm first when there are unsaved changes.

`href(location)` from `alinea`: the href of the same locations, for a link that also opens in a new tab: `<a href={href({entryId: post.id})}>`. It is a plain function, so it also works in table rows, in the `help` of a field and on the server, where you prefix the dashboard's url: `${baseUrl}/admin${href({entryId})}`.
`usePreviewMetadata()`: the title, description and other metadata the live preview reports for the current page.
Components and types:
`FieldChrome`: the label, help text and error of a field around your own control.

`EditField`, `EditFields`: render a field, or a record of fields, with the view it is configured with, for example to lay out existing fields in a `Field.view` section. Pass an object field to `EditFields` to render its fields, or some of them, in the scope of the object: `<EditFields field={Product.dimensions} fields={{width: Product.dimensions.width}} />`.
`EntryTable`: a table of entries with the columns of an
overview
, for example to list related entries in a `Field.view` section.
`FieldViewProps<F>`, `SectionViewProps`, `TypeViewProps`, `RootViewProps`: the props the dashboard passes to a field view, a `Field.view` component, a type's `view` and a root's `view`.

`OverviewCellProps`, `OverviewActionProps`, `OverviewEntry`: the props of an overview column's `view` and of an overview action, and the entry they receive. `EntryActionProps` and `DashboardEntry`: the props of an entry action and the entry `useEntry()` returns.
Show a component between fields
`Field.view` adds a component to a type that doesn't store a value, for example to show instructions or information derived from the entry. Spread it into `fields`:
Replace the form of a type

A type's `view` replaces the form of its entries with your own component, for example to edit the fields in a layout of your own. The entry header stays above it, with the title, the status, the publish and draft buttons, the type's `actions` and the sidebar with history and references. The view fills the rest of the editor, without padding.

The view receives `TypeViewProps`: the `type` of the entry. It edits the entry like the form does: the field hooks, `EditField` and `EditFields` read and write the fields of the entry, the changes show up as unsaved edits in the header and are kept until the editor publishes or saves a draft, and leaving the entry with unsaved changes asks to confirm first. To fill the editor, size the view with `height: 100%`.
Add actions to the entry header

Buttons that act on the entry, such as an export or a button that creates a related entry, go in the `actions` of its type. They render in the entry header next to the publish button and receive `EntryActionProps`: the `entry` and the `locale` it is edited in. The hooks of `alinea/cms` read and write its fields.
Upgrading from Alinea 1.x
Field views from 1.x keep working, with deprecated APIs:

`useField` from `alinea/dashboard` returns `{value, mutator, options, label, error}`. Replace it with the tuple `useField` from `alinea/cms` and the separate `useFieldOptions` and `useFieldError`. `useFieldValue`, `useFieldOptions`, `useFieldError` and `useFieldKey` also move to `alinea/cms`, and `useFieldMutator` becomes `useFieldSetter`.

`InputLabel` from `alinea/dashboard` is now the `Field` component. It no longer shows `help` from `{...options}`: use `FieldChrome` from `alinea/cms`, which reads it from the field, or pass the help text to `Field` from `alinea/components` as `description`.
`useLocale`, `useGraph` and `useEntryEditor` from `alinea/dashboard/hook/*` become `useLocale`, `useGraph` and `useEntry` from `alinea/cms`.

`useEntryEditor` still works as a shim for views that only read the entry: `activeVersion` has the `id`, `locale`, `path`, `status`, `title` and `type` of the entry, and `activeVersion.data` only has `path`. Reading another field of it throws, read field values with `useFieldValue(field)` instead. `useEntry()` returns the same entry as a `DashboardEntry`, with its saved field values in `data`.
Hooks imported from `alinea/dashboard/hooks` still work, but that module is internal: import them from `alinea/cms`.
Components from `alinea/ui` were removed. Use
`alinea/components`
See
Upgrading from 1.x
for the other dashboard changes.
